A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fastMU research. All 26 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including figures, equations, references and appendices, support comparison. The mathematical and experimental revisions can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic experiments, parameter tuning, and evaluations on MAPS audio and Urban hyperspectral data, including NMF and fixed-factor NLS results.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original synthetic, tuning, audio and hyperspectral experiments, with results for the revised fastMU method and its comparators.

M1.justification: The Frobenius preconditioner changes from the data-dependent construction in v1 Equation (29) to Diag(WW^T1) in v2 Equation (25), using a constant-vector optimizer. This changes the update procedure; the principal KL preconditioner remains equivalent. v2 also removes the extrapolated Frobenius and approximate-Hessian KL variants.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NMF and fixed-factor NLS on the same synthetic data families, four dense/sparse KL scenarios, MAPS audio excerpt and Urban hyperspectral image. The added discussion of sparsity and residuals does not introduce another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The plotted external baselines remain MU, HALS, NeNMF and GD for Frobenius loss, and MU for KL. The comparisons remove fastMU_Fro_ex and fastMU_KL_approx. Section 5.2.1 additionally reports a qualitative KL comparison in which GD was unreasonably slow.

E3.justification: The stated data generation, dimensions, ranks, SNRs, loss normalization, initialization and stopping rules remain unchanged. Figure 3 retains the same SNR-to-row assignment when inspected visually. Different displayed time windows do not establish changed execution budgets.

E4.justification: v2 removes the investigations of whether extrapolation accelerates Frobenius optimization and whether the approximate KL Hessian remains reliable under sparsity. These included substantial comparisons and failure analyses in v1 Sections 4.3–5.2. The inner-stopping parameter sweep and dense/sparse evaluations of the retained method remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 3 newly specifies 10 realizations, whereas v1 supplies only the general default of five for that experiment. Figure 7's caption changes from five experiments to P=10, but the real-data discussion still states P=5. These are reporting changes; a consistent increase in executed runs cannot be established. Median and individual-run reporting otherwise remain.

E6.justification: Figures 3–10 lose the complete result series for the discarded variants, including the approximate KL variant's sparse-case failures and dense-case speed advantage. The synthetic Frobenius discussion consequently identifies NeNMF alone instead of NeNMF and extrapolated fastMU as the best performers. Figure 2 changes the reported best delta interval from [0.01, 0.1] to [0.05, 0.1], and v2 adds the poor KL-GD finding.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the relaxed optimization and proof in Proposition 2 with a proof that a constant vector minimizes the original sum of diagonal majorant entries for strictly positive symmetric B. Remark 1 and the new minmax appendix derive the alternative eigenvector solution and its connection to gradient descent. v2 also corrects the quadratic expansion's linear-term sign and Proposition 1's positive-definite assertion to positive semidefinite.

C1.justification: The conclusion changes a central claim: v1 explicitly says its chosen majorant is not the best in the family, whereas v2 claims optimality under the selected criterion. v2 withdraws the extrapolated-variant contribution and adds an introductory qualification about sparse data and large residuals. The abstract softens its speedup wording, although the introduction retains the orders-of-magnitude claim.

C2.justification: v2 explains that sparsifying observations creates larger residuals and uses sparse audio versus dense hyperspectral data to interpret the KL results. This replaces v1's emphasis on large datasets and high rank as directions needing investigation. Remark 1 also interprets the majorant choices through average versus worst-direction curvature.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the inner-update indexing and explicitly requires epsilon-positive initialization. v2 removes implementation guidance for approximate-Hessian precomputation and extrapolation, including its special stepsize. The repository reference, software tools and retained preprocessing and tuning information remain available in both PDFs.

R1.justification: Four extrapolation-related references disappear: Ang and Gillis, Beck and Teboulle, Botev and colleagues, and O'Donoghue and Candes. v2 explicitly attributes Proposition 1's inspiration to Lee and Seung's convergence proof. The broader positioning relative to MU, HALS and NeNMF remains stable.

P1.justification: The six-section narrative remains recognizable. v2 edits language, notation and affiliations, adds keywords, consolidates Section 4.3 around dynamic stopping, and revises the method and results prose to reflect the scientific changes. It also adds the minmax appendix without broadly reorganizing the paper.

P2.justification: All ten figure identities remain, but plots are substantially reduced and regrouped with other figures or prose. Legends and several axis ranges or scales change. The resulting layout is more compact, but smaller plot labels reduce readability, and captions for Figures 1, 2 and 7–10 incorrectly describe side-by-side panels as top/bottom.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces an explicitly suboptimal majorant construction with a proved solution to the selected optimization criterion and corrects important mathematical errors, strengthening the core derivation. The overall gain is moderated by smaller plots, incorrect panel-orientation captions and inconsistent run-count reporting. The empirical coverage and broad performance conclusions remain largely unchanged.
